chunks: Yūnus narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him and said to him, ‘May I be your ransom, what is the blood money for the child of zinā?’ He said, ‘The one who spent on him is given what he spent on him.’ I said, ‘If he dies and has wealth, then who inherits him?’ He said, ‘The Imam.’
And it has also been narrated that the blood money for the child of zinā is eight hundred dirhams, and his inheritance is like the inheritance of the child of mulāʿanah.

key_terms.ابْنِ الْمُلَاعَنَةِ: the child of mulāʿanah, used here as a legal comparison
key_terms.الْإِمَامُ: the Imam as the inheritor in this ruling
key_terms.ثَمَانُمِائَةِ دِرْهَمٍ: eight hundred dirhams as the specified amount of blood money
key_terms.دِيَةُ وَلَدِ الزِّنَا: the blood money due in the case of a child born out of fornication
key_terms.مَالٌ: property or wealth left by the deceased
key_terms.وَلَدِ الزِّنَا: a child born out of zinā

ai.seo_question: What is the diyyah and inheritance ruling for a child born out of zinā in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on the blood money and inheritance of a child born out of zinā. It states that compensation goes to the one who spent on the child, that the Imam inherits the child’s estate in one report, and also cites another report specifying eight hundred dirhams and comparing the inheritance ruling to that of the child of mulāʿanah.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications:
Hadith.5682 - Yunus narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:
I asked Imam (as): "May I be your ransom, what is the blood money (diyyah) for a child born out of fornication?"
Imam (as) replied: "The one who spent on him is to be given what he spent on him."
I asked: "If the child dies and has wealth, who inherits it?"
He (as) said: "The Imam."
It has also been narrated: "The blood money (diyyah) for a child born out of fornication is eight hundred dirhams, and his inheritance is like the inheritance of the child of mula'anah (mutual cursing between spouses in the case of adultery accusations)."
